tenancy_law.rule: Rent increases must be reasonable and subject to mutual agreement. Unilateral increases without notice are generally unenforceable. Courts have held that increases beyond 10-15% per annum without justification are unconscionable.
tenancy_law.negotiation_tip: Negotiate a fixed rent review cap tied to Nigeria's CPI/inflation rate, not landlord discretion. A mutual 90-day notice period is standard.

tenancy_law.statute: Common Law & Lagos State Tenancy Law 2011
tenancy_law.rule: The Landlord is responsible for all external, structural, and major repairs. This includes the roof, load-bearing walls, foundation, and external plumbing. A clause shifting this burden to the tenant without compensatory rent reduction is void.
tenancy_law.negotiation_tip: Reject clauses that assign structural repairs to the Tenant. If accepted, negotiate a significant rent reduction or a one-time capital allowance.

tenancy_law.statute: Recovery of Premises Act Cap R4 LFN 2004 & Lagos State Tenancy Law 2011
tenancy_law.rule: A yearly tenant is entitled to 6 months' notice to quit. A half-yearly tenant gets 3 months, a quarterly tenant gets 1.5 months, and a monthly tenant gets 1 month. Any clause waiving this statutory right is void and unenforceable.
tenancy_law.negotiation_tip: Ensure the notice period in the contract aligns with the Recovery of Premises Act. Do not sign any clause that says the Landlord can require immediate vacation.

tenancy_law.statute: Recovery of Premises Act & Criminal Code Act
tenancy_law.rule: Self-help eviction (locking the tenant out, removing belongings) is illegal in Nigeria. The Landlord must obtain a court order. A clause purporting to authorize self-help eviction is void.
tenancy_law.negotiation_tip: Flag any clause that allows the Landlord to 're-enter' the premises without a court order. This is a criminal offense under Nigerian law.

commercial_law.statute: Nigerian Contract Law (Common Law principles applied by Nigerian courts)
commercial_law.rule: A clause is a void penalty if it imposes a payment on breach disproportionate to the innocent party's loss. Only 'Liquidated Damages' — a genuine pre-estimate of loss — are enforceable. Nigerian courts consistently strike down punitive penalties.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Replace 'penalty' with 'Liquidated Damages' language. Both parties should agree on a reasonable daily rate tied to actual project costs, not a punitive multiplier.

commercial_law.statute: Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020, Section 301
commercial_law.rule: Any provision exempting a company director from liability for negligence or breach of duty is void. A one-sided indemnity that only protects the Landlord exposes the Tenant to unlimited risk and is contrary to natural justice principles applied by Nigerian courts.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Demand mutual indemnity clauses. Any waiver of rights for 'Landlord negligence' must be removed — this is a void provision under CAMA 2020 principles.
red_flags: waives all rights to claim damages

commercial_law.rule: Copyright ownership initially vests in the author/creator. For commissioned works, an explicit written assignment is required to transfer full ownership. A vague 'work-for-hire' clause may not transfer copyright under the Nigerian Copyright Act 2022.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Ensure the IP clause explicitly states: (a) what IP is being assigned, (b) that it covers future works created during the contract, and (c) that you retain your pre-existing tools, frameworks, and background IP.

commercial_law.statute: Standard Nigerian Commercial Practice & Common Law
commercial_law.rule: Contracts should provide mutual termination rights. A clause allowing only the stronger party (e.g., Landlord or Client) to terminate at will, while locking in the other party, creates an unconscionable imbalance that courts may refuse to enforce.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Insist on a mutual 30-day 'termination for convenience' clause. If the other party terminates early, you should be entitled to pro-rata payment for work done plus a break fee.

commercial_law.rule: A clause specifying a foreign jurisdiction (e.g., UK, US) for dispute resolution for a contract fully performed in Nigeria is practically unenforceable and extremely costly to litigate. The new Nigerian Arbitration and Conciliation Act 2023 promotes local arbitration.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Ensure the governing law is 'Federal Republic of Nigeria' and dispute resolution specifies Lagos Multi-Door Courthouse (LMDC) or Lagos Court of Arbitration (LCA) for cost-effective resolution.
red_flags: governed by the laws of england

commercial_law.statute: Nigerian Contract Law & Restraint of Trade Doctrine
commercial_law.rule: An overly broad non-compete clause is unenforceable in Nigeria if it is unreasonable as to geographic scope, time duration, or the activity restricted. Nigerian courts will not enforce restraints that effectively prevent a person from earning a living.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Non-compete clauses should be limited to 6-12 months, within a defined geographic radius, and restricted to only directly competing businesses — not entire industries.
red_flags: shall not engage in any business

commercial_law.rule: A clause imposing mandatory purchase minimums backed by automatic shortfall penalty fees or cascade termination is an illegal penalty clause under Nigerian law unless tied to genuine pre-estimated losses.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Cap shortfall fees to actual documented losses, insert a grace period, and permit shortfall carrying-forward to future quarters.
red_flags: penalty fee for failure to purchase

commercial_law.rule: Romalpa-style clauses granting immediate forfeiture or repossession of delivered goods upon minor payment default create high risk for distributors and may violate Nigerian equity principles.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Insist on written notice of default with a minimum 14-day cure period before repossession or title forfeiture rights trigger.

commercial_law.statute: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA) 2018
commercial_law.rule: Automatic renewal by silence or deemed acceptance of unilateral price changes without explicit affirmative written consent is unfair under Nigerian consumer and commercial protection standards.
commercial_law.negotiation_tip: Require written notice 30 days prior to any renewal or price adjustment, with explicit opt-out rights.

employment_law.rule: Under the Nigerian Labour Act, a worker is entitled to minimum notice before termination (1 day for daily workers, 1 week for monthly workers, etc). Summary dismissal is only justified for gross misconduct. Contracts cannot lawfully exclude this right.
employment_law.negotiation_tip: Ensure your employment contract specifies at least 1-month notice for senior roles, and clearly defines what constitutes 'gross misconduct' to avoid arbitrary termination.

employment_law.statute: Labour Act Cap L1 LFN 2004, Section 7
employment_law.rule: Deductions from wages are only lawful if authorized by statute, court order, or written agreement with the employee specifying the purpose. Unauthorized deductions constitute a criminal offence under the Labour Act.
employment_law.negotiation_tip: Do not sign any clause allowing blanket deductions. Any deduction clause must specify the exact amount, purpose, and your right to dispute.
